prompt:
Write a clinical treatment summary (about 150 words) by the treating provider for a patient with wrist fracture after a hit while turning left. The patient had 16 visits. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1233; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The injury does not fit the crash: the impact was very light, yet the claimed injury is severe.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Nearly all findings rest on the patient's own pain reports; imaging and exam tests are normal.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- The bills show no repeated charges.
text: Patient presented following a collision sustained while turning left, reporting wrist pain and a claimed fracture of the wrist. Over sixteen visits, care followed a conventional course, with frequency tapering as symptoms were reported to improve. Radiographic studies and clinical examination were within normal limits, and the wrist findings documented here rest almost entirely on the patient's subjective pain reports. Per the history obtained, there is no known prior injury to the same area. The description of the impact indicates a low-energy event, which does not clearly correspond to the severity of the injury being claimed. Billing records reviewed for this episode show no duplicated or repeated charges for the same services. Recommend continued clinical correlation and reassessment if new objective findings emerge.
